steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Food Safety Act 1990 is the key UK legislation: it requires food businesses to ensure food is safe, not harmful to health, and labelled accurately.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Under the Food Safety Act, it is an offence to sell food that is unfit for human consumption, or to describe food falsely (e.g. mislabelling).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Environmental Health Officers (EHOs) enforce food safety law: they inspect premises, take food samples, issue improvement notices, and can close businesses that pose a health risk.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: EHOs inspect food businesses unannounced and assess hygiene based on: food handling, physical condition of premises, and confidence in management.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the three main requirements of the Food Safety Act 1990? | Q: What is the role of an Environmental Health Officer? | Q: What does HACCP stand for?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Food must be safe to eat, not harmful to health, and labelled and described accurately (not misleadingly). | EHOs enforce food safety law by inspecting food premises (often unannounced), taking food samples, issuing improvement notices, and closing businesses that pose an immediate health risk. | Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the 7 HACCP principles in order — examiners often ask you to list or apply them. Always give three types of hazard (biological, chemical, physical) with specific examples when discussing HACCP. When asked about legislation, name the specific Act (Food Safety Act 1990) and state its key requirements. For due diligence, explain it is a legal defence that requires documented evidence of all reasonable precautions.
